title: Fast Path to Prod: Hosted API messaging and pricing options
summary: Working brief for developer-focused Hosted API messaging: three concise value props, three quickstart entry angles, and draft pricing language variants for homepage, signup flows, and docs. Purpose: produce copy for marketing pages + A/B testable pricing lines for q4 launch.
audience: Primary: software and ML engineers evaluating APIs to ship LLM features. Secondary: platform teams and engineering managers who care about cost predictability and SLOs.
top_value_props: Developer-first: integrate in minutes with SDKs, examples, and a sandbox. Focus on code, not infra.
Predictable performance: SLO-backed low-latency tiers and model profiles so you build with consistent tail latency in mind.
Cost controls for production: batching, KV/prefix caching, and per-route unit metrics that let teams optimize cost without blind tradeoffs on quality.
quickstart_angles: Zero-to-hello-world (60s): npm install + single API call sample that streams token-level events to the browser. Goal: measurable time-to-first-success for devs.
Prototype-to-production (20 min): start with sandbox keys, import model presets, flip on autoscaling, and enable a cost alert rule. Demo repo shows local dev -> hosted with canary rollout config.
Platform-onramp (for infra owners): show dedicated capacity upgrade path and private deployment checklist. Emphasize identical API surface across hosted -> dedicated -> private.
pricing_language_variants: Commit & save: reserve monthly capacity for predictable throughput and up to 40% discounted unit price.
Transparent unit economics: list typical per-token costs for short/medium/long sequences and include a cost-savings calculator (batching + cache scenarios).
Fail-safe billing: tiered limits and automatic cap to prevent runaway charges; explicit developer-facing budget controls in the console.
competitive_notes: OpenAI-style APIs: great for speed of adoption but weaker on hosting guarantees and enterprise routing/rollouts. Key distinction: our emphasis on production SLOs and predictable economics.

Cloud vendor endpoints (GCP/AWS): strong infra but slower developer UX for model experimentation and fewer built-in inference optimizations. Positioning: faster dev iteration + tuned runtime for open models.

Self-hosted inference stacks: lower per-unit cost in some cases but high ops burden. Angle: offer the same API ergonomics with optional Dedicated/Private paths so teams can start hosted and migrate without code changes.
differentiation_highlights: Unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private – same client, same rollout model, predictable behavior.
Observability-first: token-level latency + cost breakdowns exposed in the console and SDK traces.
Smart routing & graceful fallback: automated fallbacks to cheaper model variants under load while maintaining functional correctness.
open_questions: Homepage price line: should we show a single starter unit price or a range (short/long) to avoid surprises?
Free sandbox limits: token cap per month vs session-based ephemeral keys — which reduces fraud while maximizing trial utility?
Embeddings pricing: per-vector vs per-token hybrid? Need input from infra on cost-per-90k-dim operation.
Legal/compliance language for enterprise billing and data retention in the default hosted tier.
recommended_next_steps: Draft three homepage hero variants that map to the three quickstart angles and run 2-week headline A/B tests.
Create a tiny demo repo (hosted-api-hello-prod) that showcases 60s and 20-min flows; instrument time-to-first-success metric.
Sync with infra and pricing ops to finalize per-token examples for short (<=128), medium (512), long (2k+) sequences.
Legal review for billing and sandbox terms; draft developer-friendly TOS snippet for signup flow.
Prepare a one-pager for sales enabling: when to upsell Dedicated vs advise Hosted.
